Introduction

Section 1The opportunity

Many organisations want the protection that Microsoft 365 sensitivity labels provide — classification, encryption, controlled sharing and an audit trail — but adoption stalls. The labels exist in the tenant, yet the material that matters stays scattered across hundreds of SharePoint sites and personal OneDrive accounts, unlabelled and unprotected. The usual reason is not unwillingness: it is that protected and convenient normally pull in opposite directions.

MOSE — Move to Security — closes that gap from both ends. It gives your administrators a guided way to create protected areas, to deliver those areas straight into the right people's File Explorer, and to find and consolidate sensitive content into them, so a label is applied automatically the moment content arrives. What is normally a manual, error-prone project becomes a repeatable, auditable workflow.

In one sentence: MOSE creates secure SharePoint areas whose documents are labelled on arrival and appear automatically in members' OneDrive, then helps you search or browse the whole tenant and move approved content into them.

Why the "secure area" is more than a folder

A MOSE secure area is not one site — it is a small structure that mirrors how work actually runs. Each area carries a set of stages, and every stage is its own SharePoint site and document library, with its own permissions, its own sensitivity label and its own auto-sync setting. The area team is applied to every stage; a sensitive stage — costing, contract, medical, personal data — can be restricted to a smaller group without touching the rest of the area.

That structure is what lets one tool serve a bid, a project, a case or a customer engagement: the same area holds the open working material and the confidential material, correctly separated, without anyone maintaining two places to look.

Introduction
The opportunity — at a glance
Today, sensitive material sits unlabelled across the tenant. MOSE consolidates it into a secure area whose every stage is a separate labelled site — so the label applies on arrival and the most sensitive stages stay restricted to the few.
Nothing new for people to learn. The stages a person is on appear in their ordinary File Explorer under OneDrive. They open, edit and save as usual; the protection travels with the file. Section 3 covers how that delivery works and where its limits are.

Why Langate

MOSE is built on the same Microsoft 365 platform and the same shared component library that power Langate's established products. SharePoint access, tenant search, site provisioning, people pickers, sensitivity-label handling, translation and error reporting are all long-standing, production-hardened building blocks rather than new code written for this proposal. That is what shortens the path to production — and it is why the parts of MOSE that had to be written new could be given the attention that a destructive, tenant-wide tool deserves.

It is your tenant, end to end

Both components run inside your own Microsoft 365 tenant and Azure subscription. Content is read, indexed and moved in place — nothing is copied to Langate, and Microsoft remains your only sub-processor.

Built to fail safe, not to look good

Every uncertain answer resolves the cautious way: an unreadable hold status blocks the move, an unverified copy preserves the original, and a partly-failed run reports its failures rather than painting success.

Solution

Section 2What MOSE does

Four capabilities, used in this order. The first two set up protection; the last two fill it with the content that belongs there.

1Create a secure area

Name the area and its customer, pick the team, review the stages — then Create. MOSE provisions one SharePoint site and document library per stage, sets each library's default sensitivity label, and applies the team's permissions. Everything added afterwards is labelled on arrival, with no per-file action.

2Deliver it to the team

Each stage can auto-sync: its library appears by itself in members' OneDrive and File Explorer — nobody clicks Sync. People receive only the stages they are on, files stay cloud-resident until opened, and joining or leaving an area adds or removes the folder automatically.

3Find the content

Two ways. Search the tenant for the words that describe sensitive material — SharePoint always, plus OneDrive and Exchange when authorised. Or Select: browse a live tree of every site, library, folder and file, and tick what you want.

4Move it to security

You review exactly what will change, then confirm. MOSE copies, verifies the copy, applies the label and only then removes the original, and writes every action to an audit trail. Items on legal hold are never moved, and the result is reported honestly: Moved · Skipped · Failed.

A worked example

A bid manager creates the area Harbour Terminal Retrofit for customer Meridian Ports AB and adds the bid team. MOSE provisions four stage sites — Qualification, Costing & margins, Customer proposal, Contract & signature — and gives each its label. Costing and Contract are restricted to three people; the other two go to the whole team. Within minutes each member finds the stages they are entitled to in their own File Explorer.

The manager then searches the tenant for Meridian, terminal, tender, margin, reviews what comes back, selects what belongs in the bid and confirms the move — the material lands in the right stage, protected on arrival. Anything the search misses can be picked by hand in the Select tree.

Folder-level intelligence: when a folder contains a match, MOSE offers the whole folder and states how many non-matching files would travel with it — so related material is not left behind and nothing moves unnoticed.
The person stays in control. MOSE discovers and suggests; a human selects and confirms. Nothing moves autonomously, and the riskiest scopes require a second approver.

How it works — four steps

What MOSE is not

Being precise about the boundary is part of the offer:

  • It is not a label-policy designer. MOSE uses the sensitivity labels your tenant already publishes — it reads your own label catalogue and never invents a taxonomy of its own.
  • It is not a data-loss-prevention scanner. Discovery finds indexed, text-bearing content matching the keywords you choose; it does not claim to locate every sensitive item in the tenant (see Section 6).
  • It is not a backup or archive tool. A move relocates content — with verification and an audit record, but it is a move.

What an area usually maps to

The stage template is yours to define, so the same structure serves very different work. Four patterns we see:

AreaTypical stages
A bid or tenderQualification · Costing & margins (restricted) · Customer proposal · Contract & signature (restricted)
A projectPlanning · Design · Delivery · Commercial (restricted)
A case or matterIntake · Working file · Legal correspondence (restricted) · Closure
A standing categoryA single stage is perfectly valid — an area with one labelled library, for e.g. board papers or personnel files.
Every area is separate by construction. Because a stage is its own SharePoint site, closing an engagement means retiring its own sites — not unpicking a shared library that four other teams also use.

Product tour · Step 2Stages & team

Opening an area shows what it is made of. Each stage names its real SharePoint site and library, who can reach it, its sensitivity label and whether it auto-syncs. Changes save to your MOSE lists immediately; lowering a stage's label warns you first that it would widen access.

Provisioning is asynchronous and honest about it. The area is ordered from the dashboard and built by the background engine — normally within a minute per stage. A freshly created SharePoint site can take up to about 15 minutes before Microsoft accepts its default label, so MOSE keeps the area marked getting ready, with a live timer, until every label is confirmed applied — and only then emails the members. An area is never presented as protected before it is.

Solution · product tour

Product tour · Step 3Search the tenant

Search runs from inside the destination area, so the question is always "what belongs in this area?". Keywords are matched on any or all words, and the scope is explicit.

Two deliberate limits on the elevated scopes

  • Email is never moved — it is labelled where it stands. The message stays in the mailbox and keeps its attachments; what changes is that the message and every attachment that can carry a classification now do. An attachment of a type Microsoft 365 cannot label (a photo, a text file, an archive) is left untouched and reported as such, never quietly passed over. Mailbox search is treated as a personal-data matter and is gated accordingly.
  • A photo becomes a record, never a loose image. A picture moved out of OneDrive does not arrive in the secure area as a picture: it arrives as a PDF record carrying the image, its capture date, its location and who owned it. A raw photo cannot hold a classification, so moving one as-is would put ungoverned content in the governed library.

Solution · product tour

Product tour · Step 4Browse and pick

Sometimes you know where the material is and would rather point at it. The Select tab is a live tree of the tenant — sites, document libraries, folders, files — already expanded when you open it, with real sizes and counts on every branch.

It shows the whole tenant, not a fraction

The tree is built from MOSE's own continuously refreshed inventory rather than SharePoint search. A picker built on search shows only sites the person has opened and the index has caught up with — on our test tenant that was 12 sites out of 22. MOSE lists them all.

It hides what you could never use

SharePoint's own plumbing — Style Library, Site Assets, Site Pages, the galleries — is excluded, and in every language, because MOSE reads the markers SharePoint sets rather than matching English names. Personal OneDrive sites and unreadable container sites are left out too.

Ticking a folder takes everything inside it; a partly-picked folder shows a half-tick. Picked items are queued to the area, where the same mandatory review-and-confirm governs the actual move.

Solution · product tour

Product tour · Step 5Photos become records

A secure area holds records, not loose files. So when a photo is moved in — JPG, PNG, HEIC, BMP — MOSE does not copy the photo across. It builds a stamped PDF record of that photo and moves that instead.

There is a hard technical reason as well as a governance one: a raw JPEG is not a file type Microsoft 365 can label. A photo copied into a secure area would sit there carrying the library's permissions but no protection of its own — governed by where it happens to be, and unprotected the moment it is copied out. A PDF can carry the label, so the record is protected on arrival like everything else.

What arrives in the secure area
Only the PDF arrives. The photograph itself never reaches the secure area at all — which is the point: what lands there is a governed record, not an unprotectable blob.

Two cases MOSE refuses rather than gets wrong

Files that hold more than one page

An animated GIF, or a multi-page TIFF scan. A record shows one picture, so converting would keep the first frame — and the move would then delete the original for good. Those pages would be gone with nothing to recover them. MOSE reports the item failed and leaves it exactly where it is, saying why.

Photos that cannot be converted

Corrupt files, or a HEIC that SharePoint has not finished preparing. The item is reported failed and the original is untouched; run it again later. MOSE never falls back to copying the raw photo in — that would put an ungoverned file in the governed library precisely when nobody is watching.

It is a switch, not a law. An administrator can turn the conversion off, in which case photos move intact like any other file. That is a deliberate decision to take the originals — and it is the only way MOSE will ever place an unlabellable file in a secure area.

Auto-sync to OneDrive

Section 3Protection people actually use

A secure area that people have to remember to visit is a secure area they will work around. MOSE therefore delivers each stage into the place they already work: File Explorer, under OneDrive.

How the delivery works

MOSE pushes a OneDrive sync-client policy through Intune that names each auto-sync stage library. The client silently signs in, mounts the libraries the person is entitled to, and keeps files cloud-resident until opened. No device is touched by hand and nobody clicks Sync.

Auto-sync to OneDrive

What the team experiences

BehaviourWhat it means in practice
Access-gatedThe policy may offer several libraries; a person only ever mounts the ones they have permission to. Verified live: three libraries offered, only the one the user was a member of appeared.
Follows the personA member with two or three PCs gets the folder on all of them. Verified live on separate devices.
Joining and leavingAdding someone to an area brings the folder to their PC on the sync client's next evaluation; removing them takes it away.
Light on diskFiles On-Demand is required by the policy, so a mounted library costs almost no local storage.
Know the edge of this feature. Intune reaches enrolled Windows PCs. It does nothing for the browser, for phones, or for an unenrolled machine — there, the same library is one click away via a shortcut link instead. Auto-sync is a convenience layer on top of permissions: it can deliver a folder, and it can never widen who may open it.
One tenant setting we recommend but will not change for you: co-authoring for files with sensitivity labels. Without it, only one person at a time can edit an encrypted file in the Office desktop apps. With it, a labelled, encrypted, synced document behaves like any other shared file. It is an effectively one-way, tenant-wide change, so a compliance administrator makes that call once — we provide the exact steps.

Two details worth deciding early

  • PDFs need one extra tenant switch before the library's default label covers them; without it, Office files in a secure library are labelled and PDFs quietly are not. The installer can set it for you, and it is reversible. Note that signed and password-protected PDFs can never be labelled by SharePoint.
  • Who receives which area. By default one policy carries every area's libraries to one audience, so a person may be offered a library they cannot open. Mapping each area to its own group keeps that tidy — you create the groups, MOSE never manages groups across your directory.

Delivery & scope

Section 4How we deliver

Architecture

MOSE is two deployables that share one code base, both running inside your tenant:

  • The dashboard — a SharePoint Framework (SPFx) web part on a MOSE administration site, where areas are created, stages managed, content searched or browsed, and moves approved.
  • The engine — an Azure Function that performs every privileged action. The dashboard never moves content itself: it asks the engine, which enforces the safety rules regardless of what asked it to act.
Engine endpointWhat it does
GET /api/healthIs the engine alive and fully configured? Returns no secrets.
POST /api/labelsReads your tenant's own sensitivity labels so the dashboard can offer them by name. Read-only.
POST /api/discoveryRuns a saved search under the discovery identity. Discovery only — that identity holds no Graph write permission, and every move, label and delete goes through Graph, so it is unable to move anything.
POST /api/provisionCreates a stage's site and library and sets its default label.
POST /api/moveThe move. Copy, verify, label, delete, audit — every gate enforced server-side.
POST /api/approveThe second half of the two-person rule: a different operator releases a dual-control move.

Four background timers keep the system current: provisioning (builds ordered areas and re-applies any label a new site was not yet ready to accept), inventory (refreshes the tenant content map every five minutes via SharePoint's own change log), notifications, and an optional photo-to-PDF intake.

There is no scheduled content search. Discovery runs only when an operator starts it — a tenant-wide search is an elevated act and should have a person's name against it, not a timer's.

Installation — one command

MOSE ships as a single PowerShell installer plus two build artifacts. It installs its own prerequisites, then runs ten phases in dependency order — tooling, sign-in, capability gate, management app, dashboard package, administration site and its lists, the web part, the three identities with certificates in Key Vault, the Function with sign-in protection, the OneDrive policy — and finishes with a health check that must report healthy before it declares success.

It refuses to start what it cannot finish. The capability gate checks every permission the run needs before the first change, so you are never left half-provisioned. -WhatIf prints the entire plan without touching anything, and the installer is idempotent — re-running it reuses what exists.

PrerequisiteWhy, and what happens without it
A licence covering "default sensitivity labelling for a SharePoint document library" This is what makes content protected on arrival. Delivery & scope

Section 4bWhere the product stands

MOSE is a new product approaching release. We would rather you knew exactly what is proven today than discover the boundary later, so this page states it plainly. The screenshots in this document are of the running build described here — nothing in this quotation is a mock-up.

Proven on a live tenant

  • The move — copy, verify, label, remove the source, write the audit record — verified end to end against a real tenant, and checked against the tenant itself rather than against MOSE's own report of what it did.
  • Installation — the single-command installer has run end-to-end on a fresh tenant and subscription to a verified healthy state.
  • Area provisioning — stage sites and libraries are created, permissioned and labelled; areas stay gated until every label is confirmed, then email their members in each recipient's own language.
  • Auto-sync — the full chain (policy push → Intune → device → mounted library) is proven on real devices, including access-gating and multiple PCs per person.
  • Tenant inventory — the five-minute content map is proven against live changes: additions, renames and deletions are each reflected correctly.
  • The dashboard — creation, stage administration, search setup and the Select tree all run against live tenant data, covered by an automated end-to-end suite. A stage's label is chosen from your own tenant's labels, by name, with warnings before you lower one or add encryption.

Completing before go-live

  • Your first move, on your content. The move itself is proven end to end on our test tenant: an automated test creates real content, orders an area, waits for it to be built, moves the files, and then inspects the tenant rather than believing what MOSE reported — sources gone, copies intact and labelled, a signpost left behind, a governance record written. What remains is the first run against your content and scale, which is deliberately a supervised pilot in stage 4 of the plan, on a scope you choose.
  • Hold and retention reads depend on the one-time Purview role grant described opposite. Until it is in place, MOSE reports items as undetermined and refuses to move them.
What this means commercially. The value is available on day one; the move engine is delivered with a pilot in the plan, so its first use on your content happens with us alongside you and on a scope you set.
Ten languages. The dashboard renders in the viewer's SharePoint language and the notification emails in each recipient's own mailbox language: English, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Portuguese. Anything else falls back to English.

Security & compliance

Section 6Security & compliance

MOSE is granted broad reach over your content by design — it must be able to search widely and to move approved material. We treat that trust as the core of the engagement. This section sets out how the access is split, protected, gated and logged.

Runs inside your tenant

Both parts of MOSE are deployed into your own Microsoft 365 tenant and Azure subscription. Your content is read, indexed and moved within your tenant; it is never copied to Langate systems or any third party. Microsoft, already your cloud provider, is the only sub-processor. Data residency follows your tenant's region. MOSE's own working data — areas, stages, saved searches, the audit trail, the content inventory — lives in SharePoint lists and files on your administration site.

Three identities, least privilege each

MOSE installs three separate application identities rather than one powerful account:

IdentityPurposePermissions granted
Discovery
cannot move		 Searches for candidate content and reads hold state, then records what it found in MOSE's own list. It cannot move, label or delete anything — every one of those actions goes through Microsoft Graph, and this identity holds no Graph write permission at all. That is enforced by construction, not by policy, and our installer's test suite fails the build if a Graph write permission is ever added to it. Graph Files.Read.All, Mail.Read (both read-only); SharePoint Sites.Read.All and Sites.FullControl.All — the latter is what lets it save its own findings list, and it is a tenant-wide SharePoint permission; plus a read-only Purview role for hold state. Ask us if you would prefer this narrowed to Sites.Selected on the MOSE admin site alone.
Move engine
write		 Provisions stage sites, applies labels, performs approved moves, sends the notification emails. Graph InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send (restricted by Exchange policy to one mailbox), Sites.Selected; SharePoint Sites.FullControl.All, Sites.ReadWrite.All.
API Guards the engine's endpoints; carries the Mose.Operator role that says who may use MOSE at all. No content permissions.

Each identity authenticates with its own certificate, held in Azure Key Vault and resolved at run time by the Function's managed identity — no key material ships in the deployment package. The tenant-wide SharePoint grants on the move identity are what let it create site collections and remove source files anywhere in the tenant — the price of a tenant-wide move engine, and precisely why the searching half never holds them.

The request body is never the authority. Every privileged endpoint sits behind Microsoft sign-in and then checks the caller's validated token against the operator list. A payload can claim anything; it is never believed. An empty operator list makes the engine refuse everything rather than default open.

Security & compliance
Where MOSE runs — nothing leaves your tenant
Microsoft is the only sub-processor. Langate delivers and supports the software; your content — and MOSE's own records about it — stay inside your tenant and region.

Safe by construction

A person approves every move

MOSE discovers and suggests; a person selects and confirms against a summary of exactly what changes. Anything touching OneDrive or mailboxes, or above an agreed size, additionally requires a second operator to approve under their own sign-in. Where an organisation genuinely has only one MOSE operator, that person approves their own parked run in a separate, deliberate step — and the record says self-approved, never that two people agreed.

Copy, verify, then delete

The original is removed only after the copy is confirmed intact. If the copy or the check fails, the destination copy is rolled back and the source is left untouched — the worst case is a duplicate, never a loss.

Holds are fail-closed

If an item is on legal hold — or if MOSE cannot be certain — it is treated as held and left in place. Uncertainty never resolves in favour of moving.

No silent downgrades

A move that would lower an item's sensitivity is blocked, and one that would newly encrypt it warns first — because "protected" must not quietly mean "nobody can open it".

[CUSTOMER NAME] · MOSE Quotation
Langate
Langate · MOSE Quotation
Security & compliance
Anatomy of a safe move
The delete step is structurally unreachable until the copy has been verified and the label confirmed — a failure anywhere upstream leaves the original in place.

Audit trail

Every action — who approved it, who ran it, what moved, from where, into which area and stage, the label before and after, and what was skipped and why — is written to an append-only audit list in your tenant and can be exported. Because the work runs through SharePoint, the underlying operations are additionally recorded in your tenant's own Microsoft 365 unified audit log, so MOSE's account of itself can be checked against Microsoft's.

Honest limits

Discovery is best-effort, not a guarantee. Keyword search finds indexed, text-bearing content. Scanned images, unindexed files and material outside your chosen keywords may not surface. MOSE reduces exposure and makes it auditable — it does not claim to find every sensitive item.
A move changes access, and moves are not undone by a button. Existing sharing links to a moved item stop working — the confirm step says so explicitly, so that "now protected" never quietly means "still shared with the world". Re-share deliberately from the secure area.
A move is a redirection, not a disappearance. MOSE leaves a shortcut where the file used to be, pointing at its new home — so a bookmark or a link on a page leads somewhere instead of dying. It is a signpost, not a key: the secure area's permissions still decide who may open it, and it is written only after the copy is verified. Switchable off where a file name is itself sensitive.
Auto-sync reaches enrolled Windows PCs. A delivery convenience, not a containment control: it cannot widen access, and does not govern the browser, phones or unmanaged machines.
Before we start: a security addendum — exact permissions, a data-flow diagram, credential storage and rotation, and a Data Processing Agreement — for your security team to review alongside this quotation.
